value.body:
Design conclusions from the Manabot study, to build to (full text with evidence: ~/src/etude.exp-66-name-the-job/scratch/manabot-eval-study.md — read it). A: no-server stays the default and must not get slower. B: with a server, one worker pool serves the whole group so jobs sharing a server play at once and batch together; the server side owns how many games are active and EvalJob.workers must not multiply it. C: the handle is a picklable address; Etude never relays decisions. D: policies are unknown at server start; Etude delivers the group's checkpoints and play admits them through the handle. E: replace the match-count rule: rent for evals when the new matches are estimated at or above a threshold of machine time (from stored durations of that tournament's matches; no history means no estimate and the pass rents), or when nothing else of the experiment is queued or running; Manabot's stated target is two hours — use a reasonable default and one flag. F: one named exception for "match not played, no player at fault": leaves the match unplayed for the next pass and fails the run; a serving process that exits stops the group the same way; a refused pass must never be recorded succeeded. G: Etude sets thread-pool variables from the CPUs the container may use divided among workers, gives jobs and servers a fast local scratch directory, and retains a receipts directory for the server. H: results delivered as each match finishes; the run stops itself ahead of its deadline. I: server settings stay out of match identity. Where the base already does one of these, say so rather than rebuilding. Reasonable values for every number; do not raise them.
